assumptions: The selected c_p,s_p reference pair and Gamma_1,p=0 line are fixed independently of lambda. Changing the reference pair with lambda would change the declared domain and is outside this calculation.
The nonzero-lambda operator bound is conditional only on u having finite declared minus-tail L2(f dQ) norm; it does not construct the plus-recessive u_lambda or evaluate its actual Gamma_1 value.

Each inherited kappa bracket contains at least one zero-shell characteristic root, but uniqueness is not assumed. Every zero-shell derivative enclosure is valid for any root lying in its full bracket.
At a zero-shell root, u_0,Q(Q0)=0 and u_0(Q0) is nonzero on the whole bracket, so ODE uniqueness gives c_p=u_0/u_0(Q0).
The Mellin identity and Bessel reality/order symmetry are analytic source guards. Complex balls are retained and their imaginary intervals must contain zero.

The right contribution h(Q0) is consumed from the prior direct Green endpoint result. Subtracting it from the independently ball-evaluated full Mellin total gives an outward but correlation-forgetting left-correction enclosure.
The two precision tiers use the same locked backend and are consistency refinements, not independent implementations.

A nonzero K-scaled partial_lambda Gamma_1 enclosure at zero is a local characteristic statement for one declared extension and one explicit zero-shell representative. It does not construct a finite nonzero-lambda K-normalized family and is not a physical spectral normalization, root velocity, global measure or RAQ result.

declared_conventions.K_scaled_partial_lambda_Gamma1_at_zero: for the K-scaled zero-shell representative, partial_lambda Gamma_1|0=-u_0(Q0)*(I_total/u_0(Q0)^2); no finite nonzero-lambda K-normalized family is constructed
declared_conventions.execution: exact SymPy identities plus python-flint 0.9.0 Arb/acb elementary, Bessel and gamma balls; no ODE, quadrature, root solve, finite difference or unbounded numerical integration
declared_conventions.p_kappa_relation: kappa=sqrt(3/2)*abs(p); both p signs share the same fixed reference bound
declared_conventions.reference_equation: c_p,QQ=A_0*c_p; c_p(-4)=1 and c_p,Q(-4)=0; c_p is lambda-independent
declared_conventions.reference_tail_comparison: for y=(c_p,c_p,Q/kappa), the free part is a norm-preserving rotation and the perturbation norm is at most V/kappa with V=36*pi^4*exp(2Q)
declared_conventions.root_reference_proportionality: at any zero of u_0,Q(Q0), c_p(Q)=u_0(Q)/u_0(Q0)

exact_checks.statement: For a lambda-independent zero-energy reference c_p, W_Q(u_lambda,c_p)=-lambda*a*u_lambda*c_p.
Gamma_1=-W(-infinity)=u_Q(Q0)-lambda*integral_-infinity^Q0 a*u*c with the repository Wronskian sign.
The divided fiber forcing is a=f/2 at hbar=1.
The free-rotation perturbation integral has antiderivative 18*pi^4*exp(2Q)/kappa.
The unperturbed (c,c_Q/kappa) system is a Euclidean norm-preserving rotation.
Cauchy-Schwarz and f=2a give correction <=|lambda|*M_c/sqrt(2) per unit L2(f) norm.
The normalized declared derivative magnitude splits into the finite-Q0 right proxy contribution plus the omitted left-boundary correction.
Conditional on u_0,Q(Q0)=0 and u_0(Q0)!=0, u_0/u_0(Q0) has the declared c_p initial data (1,0), so ODE uniqueness gives c_p=u_0/u_0(Q0).
For the K-scaled zero-shell representative, partial_lambda Gamma_1|0=-u_0(Q0)*D_total and its normalization-invariant ratio is -D_total.
N_f=2*I_total reduces to sqrt(2/3)/pi times the x^(1/2) Bessel-square Mellin integral.

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: The identity and derivative concern that one declared p-preserving extension only; no physical uniqueness or p-mixing classification follows.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: The pinned raw-C extension fixes c_p(-4)=1,c_p,Q(-4)=0 and Gamma_1,p=-lim W(u,c_p), with c_p independent of lambda.

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: Gamma_1(u_lambda)=u_Q(Q0)-lambda*int a*u*c and Gamma_1,lambda(0)/u_0(Q0)=-I_total/u_0(Q0)^2; no finite nonzero-lambda Weyl value is constructed.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: u_lambda solves the divided raw-C equation, c_p solves the zero-energy reference equation, the minus Wronskian limit exists, and the lambda derivative may be passed through the weighted identity at a zero-shell root.
theorem_guards.theorem: Lagrange/Wronskian identity and differentiable plus-recessive solution family at lambda=0

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: |c_p(Q)|<=exp(18*pi^4*exp(-8)/kappa) and the reported M_c envelope bounds the entire minus tail without a cutoff or ODE calculation.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: kappa has a strictly positive full-band lower bound, V=36*pi^4*exp(2Q) is integrable on (-infinity,-4], and y=(c,c_Q/kappa) starts with unit norm at Q0.
theorem_guards.theorem: variation-of-constants/Gronwall comparison with a skew free oscillator

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: For either punctured lambda box, the reported coefficient bounds |Gamma_1-u_Q(Q0)| per unit L2(f) tail norm; it is not an actual Gamma_1 value for a constructed solution.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: u has finite declared minus-tail L2(f dQ) norm and c_p obeys the certified L2(a dQ) envelope with f=2a.

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: The full weighted K-square integral is finite and positive; subtracting the independent right Green box gives a rigorous correlation-forgetting left-correction enclosure.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: mu=3/2, nu=i*kappa, kappa real and positive, and K_(i*kappa)(x) is real for x>0.
